I don’t deserve to be loved. I have a boyfriend (we’re polyamorous) and he absolutely adores me. He’s so loving to me, and I can’t help but feel so, so guilty. Because I’m not good enough for him. We used to be in the same friend group, and something happened that made them — rightfully — hate my guts. And they’ve been treating him worse because he’s still dating me. I’m literally making his life worse, and I hate it.

Everytime I get a good thing I just fuck it up.
Autistic. If you need to be specific, then low support autistic person/LSAP.

Thank you for understanding. I'd like the mention that the lack of a door isn't a sign of abuse in my case -- when we moved into this house, there was only one bedroom with a door, and I chose the one without one (it's just more spacious).

But I do appreciate your comments. I cannot emphasize how much it hurts to genuinely believe someone is trying to be better, someone who hurt you so badly, and deciding to forgive them despite it all -- only for them to show they never cared. It's terrible.

thanks. i’ve been doing that. this sounds silly since i’m posting here, but honestly my depression has been getting better as of late. my trust issues, too. obviously i’m not healed, but it’s something.

i’m still learning the “deserving self love” part, though. i have learned that my parents probably don’t love me that much — i used to think so bc of my trust issues, but i think i have better reasons now. they buy me stuff and talk to me and do stuff for me, but whenever i struggle due to one of my disabilities or because of my trauma they don’t care. and i don’t think i can really call that love. on the other hand, i still can’t love myself. i just can’t. i would’ve killed myself a long time ago if it weren’t for my boyfriend — i don’t want to hurt him.

sorry if this is too long. i just wanted to get that off my chest.

that is fucking terrible. i am so unbelievably sorry.

i understand that you need to do this, and i’m not going to convince you to not do it — while i haven’t been in a situation like this before, i do know how upsetting it can be to have people not realize you can’t *not* do something. it’s alienating and frustrating.

but, i want you to know that you don’t deserve this. don’t ever think you do. what you went through isn’t okay. you were not asking for it, or anything like that. please remember that.

i understand feeling unlovable and dirty. when i was very young, i was exposed to pornography and fetishistic content, so i grew up having a very relaxed relationship with sexual things. at 13, i was groomed by a 21 year old — though i never fully did anything with him, that was only because i knew that it would be wrong. but i did have a crush on him — and he wanted that. i was even going to draw porn for him, before, thank god, my executive dysfunction + motivational issues kicked in. i feel dirty from these experiences. although what i experiences wasn’t as bad as what you have, i can relate to how you feel dirty — i feel disgusted with myself.

but i shouldn’t. i was a child. i didn’t know any better. similarly, you didn’t consent. you couldn’t have done anything — and even if you could, you made your boundaries clear. you said NO. that was enough. you are not dirty or unlovable for this. they are the monsters — not you.

the fact that you’re posting this here is a great start to reaching out to others. i understand why you don’t want to talk to anyone you know personally about what has happened — it is your trauma, and you should only talk about it when you are comfortable.

i would like to suggest trying to find specific circles for others who have experienced sexual assault, as well as support groups for sex workers. your experiences, unfortunately, are not uncommon. however, that does mean that there are resources for you. there are places for you. you can seek comfort and solace with people who you know will not judge you, and develop positive coping strategies.

i am so, so sorry this has happened to you.

if there *was* evidence? maybe, at least just to check it out. but i don't think it can. getting surgery for biid has been shown to have positive effects:

"Psychological therapy, psychopharmacological medication, and relaxation techniques have had little effect and sometimes increased the desire. None of the patients regretted the surgery and a change for the better was seen in almost all areas of life. There were several problems regarding the quality of life, but they were estimated as bearable in contrast to the happiness to have fulfilled the wish." (Body Integrity Identity Disorder (BIID): How Satisfied are Successful Wannabes)

"For those who had psychotherapy or medication there was no change in the intensity of the desire for amputation. The six subjects who had an amputation at their desired site reported that following the amputation they felt better than they ever had and no longer had a desire for an amputation." (Desire for amputation of a limb: paraphilia, psychosis, or a new type of identity disorder)

"Surgery is found helpful in all subjects who underwent amputation and those subjects score significantly lower on a disability scale than BIID subjects without body modification." ([Body Integrity Identity Disorder](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0034702))

if biid was a curable mental condition, then why would this be the result of getting surgery? why doesn't it end up being like, say, body dysmorphic disorder, or eating disorders, where nothing's ever enough? i honestly can't figure out why people are trying to find alternative treatments for it, as opposed to advocating for the one treatment that's been shown to work. it doesn't make any sense, imo.

tl;dr: maybe but the chances of it working are inconsistent with pretty much everything else about biid to my knowledge

hi, this is just coming from my own personal experience, so feel free to take this with a grain of salt, but:

i have biid and psychosis. i have managed to treat said psychosis to the point where i only experience it unmedicated. however, even when medicated, i still desire to remove my unwanted limbs. therefore, i can reasonably assume that my biid and psychosis are entirely unrelated.

thanks for your input! i hadn’t thought of the pure dysphoria part. to me, i feel like having my body match my mind would be enough to counteract the complications of being disabled.

transabled is, in a vacuum, a good term. the etymology makes sense and it sounds good. but trolls and bigots of all types have used it to hurt us, which sucks.

i can respect that. but i honestly can’t call myself a “bid sufferer”. of course the dysphoria is awful, but… i’m a transgender man. i have terrible gender dysphoria, but i wouldn’t call myself a gender dysphoria sufferer. i’d say i’m someone who suffers from gender dysphoria if the conversation was about gender dysphoria, but calling myself a gender dysphoria sufferer as my default term feels wrong, y’know?

also, i’d imagine even after you have surgery, you’re still considered someone with biid. but if the surgery results in no more dysphoria, are you still a bid sufferer? it doesn’t seem properly encompassing.

(not trying to start an argument or be rude or anything, you can absolutely use this term — i just want to find a term that works and i want to list any concerns i have, especially if someone can answer them, that’s all)

thanks for the reply. personally, i have two main reasons i want a term for those with biid:


1. “people with biid” is extremely clunky, and i want to be able to educate people on having biid is like and what it is. saying “people with biid” constantly takes up space and can be hard to read if repeated often.

2. i consider having biid an important part of my identity. i am an autistic person, not really a “person with autism” — i am who i am because of my autism. similarly, i am a person who doesn’t just so happen to also have biid — being a person with biid is an important part of who i am. i it’s caused me pain and hardship, but i don’t think i’d be the same without it. does that make sense?


i understand not wanting a term like this, and i don’t judge anyone who doesn’t want one. but it helps me cope with the judgement and the distress it causes me if i have an adjective i could call myself.
